name: Resistive load bank
summary: A bank of switched resistive elements used to apply a controllable test load to generators, UPS or battery systems.
description: A resistive load bank is a set of resistor elements, switched in steps and cooled by fans, used to load a generator, UPS or battery system for commissioning and maintenance tests. Permanent load banks are also installed to keep diesel engines above minimum load when site demand is low.

Drawings show a resistor symbol or a group of resistors with step switches, connected through a breaker to the bus being tested. Permanently installed banks have a control link to the genset or microgrid controller, while portable banks connect through a temporary test connection point.

A resistive bank loads at unity power factor only, so it does not test a generator at its rated kVA when the rated power factor is below one. The symbol does not show step sizes or fan supply, both needed for test planning.
readingNotes: A purely resistive bank tests kW, not kVA.
Look for a dedicated test connection point.
drawingChecklist: State kW rating and step sizes.
distinction: A resistive load bank applies only active load; a resistive-reactive bank can also apply lagging kvar.
